goal: Turn CAmount from a raw int64_t typedef into a real class so amounts can't be built from bools, floats, or mismatched integer types, or left uninitialized.
Aims to prevent a recurring class of bugs that has already bitten the project twice, and lay groundwork for a future range-bounded amount type.
reviewability: Paused. The core design (literal syntax, whether to split the PR, whether to add a bounded amount type) is still being reworked as of the latest push.
Reviewing the current diff risks being wasted since the author dropped the `_sats` literal entirely in the most recent push and reviewers have not weighed in on that since.
agreement: Disputed. Concept ACKs from sedited and ryanofsky, but l0rinc formally requested changes wanting a smaller, gradual rollout and clearer bounded-amount semantics (l0rinc).
maflcko and Sjors also suggested splitting the PR to make it reviewable (maflcko, Sjors), and optout21 and purpleKarrot pushed back on parts of the design itself (optout21, purpleKarrot).
Author has partially responded (dropped the `_sats` UDL, added scripted diffs) but the splitting request is not fully resolved.

result.summary: This RFC converts CAmount from a plain int64_t typedef into a proper C++ class across the entire codebase, disallowing implicit construction from bools/floats, uninitialized amounts, cross-type comparisons, and nonsensical amount*amount multiplication. It touches 184 files (mostly mechanical call-site updates for the new type) and evolved through 12 commits and 11 force-pushes, including scripted diffs and a literal-suffix (`_sats`) that was later replaced by a `*sats` multiplication operator. Two smaller pieces were already split off and merged (#35456, #35372).
result.problem: CAmount as a raw int64_t has caused real bugs in the past (implicit bool conversion, mismatched-width comparisons) and allows uninitialized or nonsensical amount arithmetic; this affects every area of the codebase that handles money (wallet, mempool, mining, RPC).

open_concerns: l0rinc (CHANGES_REQUESTED): wants a smaller, gradual introduction of a bounded amount type, explicit unchecked-vs-validated amount split, and clarification of AmountCompression/serialization invariants under the new type.
ryanofsky, maflcko, Sjors: PR is very large and should be split, e.g. introducing the `_sats`/unit literal or the class conversion as separate, smaller PRs.
purpleKarrot: opposes user-defined literals on principle, citing the P3045 std::quantity proposal's rejection of UDLs; prefers `*sats`-style multiplication.
optout21: prefers keeping implicit numeric convertibility and questions whether disallowing all implicit numeric interop is worth the churn; also raises separating absolute amounts from deltas.
resolved_concerns: janb84 caught and hodlinator fixed a real bug where the capnp CustomBuildField for CAmount silently failed to write values back (fixed with an added regression test).
janb84's nit about mempool_persist.cpp temporaries was addressed by switching to direct CAmount deserialization.
maflcko's LIFETIMEBOUND/const-ref question on amount.h was addressed in a later push.
hodlinator adopted ryanofsky's suggestion to use `*sats` multiplication instead of the `_sats` literal in the latest push.
discussion.author_status: active, most recently reworking core design in response to feedback (force-pushed 2026-08-25 to remove the `_sats` literal entirely)

categories.name: utils
categories.evidence: CAmount is defined in src/consensus/amount.h but functions as shared infrastructure (a core numeric primitive used across the whole node); the PR's substance is entirely about the safety semantics of this primitive type, matching utils' 'primitives first' criterion.
categories.rationale: Prevents a recurring bug class: the description cites two prior bugs (0026b330, 890a09b) caused by CAmount's loose typedef semantics, and the class design closes those holes plus uninitialized-amount and nonsensical-multiplication bugs. It is also explicitly a stepping stone toward a future range-bounded amount type, giving it leverage, but the approach itself remains disputed (see agreement).

categories.name: ipc
categories.evidence: The PR adds custom Cap'n Proto build/read field overloads for the new CAmount class and, in doing so, a reviewer (janb84) caught and the author fixed a real bug where amounts weren't actually written back to the capnp message; this is a genuine change to IPC serialization mechanics, not a mechanical call-site edit.
categories.rationale: janb84: 'Current code gets a local copy... Nothing is written back to the Cap'n Proto message,' a bug introduced and then fixed within this PR's own serialization glue for the new type, with a regression test added. Narrow in scope since it only exists because of this PR's own type change, not a pre-existing external-facing gap.

categories.name: tests
categories.evidence: Adds ConsumeMoney() overloads with a minimum-value parameter and new IPC test coverage for passing CAmount across the process boundary, which are framework-level additions rather than area-specific test pinning.
categories.rationale: The new ConsumeMoney() overload and the capnp round-trip test for CAmount (added after janb84's bug report) are minor framework additions that only exist to support this PR's own refactor, not general coverage gaps other areas were missing.

categories.name: kernel
categories.evidence: Touches kernel/bitcoinkernel.cpp, kernel/coinstats.cpp, and kernel/mempool_entry.h, but only as mechanical call-site adaptation to the new CAmount type (e.g. CheckedAdd on .Int()); no change to the kernel API surface or boundary.
categories.rationale: Not a member: the kernel-file edits are follow-on adjustments to compile against the new CAmount, not changes to what the kernel API exposes or how it behaves.

categories.name: mempool
categories.evidence: Many mempool files (txmempool.cpp/h, policy/*, mempool_entry.h) are edited, but only to adapt existing fee arithmetic to CAmount's new explicit-construction rules; no policy or acceptance-rule behavior changes.
categories.rationale: Mechanical adaptation only (e.g. UpdateModifiedFee wrapping SaturatingAdd via .Int()); mempool semantics are unchanged, so this does not meet the 'touches' bar for membership.

categories.name: mining
categories.evidence: node/miner.h, mining_types.h, and rpc/mining.cpp get default-initializers and type adjustments for CAmount fields, with no change to template construction logic.
categories.rationale: Purely mechanical follow-on edits (e.g. CAmount nFees{0};) with no behavioral change to block template assembly.

categories.name: p2p
categories.evidence: net_processing.h/.cpp changes are limited to giving CNodeStateStats::m_fee_filter_received a default initializer and fixing comparisons for the new type; no protocol or relay behavior change.
categories.rationale: Mechanical call-site fix only; does not touch relay, DoS, or connection logic.

categories.name: rpc
categories.evidence: RPC files (blockchain.cpp, mining.cpp, rawtransaction.cpp, etc.) only get amount-formatting call sites adjusted for the new type (.Int() calls, 0*sats literals); no RPC interface or return-value semantics change.
categories.rationale: No change to what any RPC method returns or accepts; purely mechanical compile-fix edits.

categories.name: tools
categories.evidence: bitcoin-tx.cpp gets a 4-line mechanical adjustment for the new CAmount type; no behavioral change to the tool.
categories.rationale: Trivial mechanical edit, not a functional change to the tool.

categories.name: validation
categories.evidence: consensus/amount.h, consensus/tx_verify.cpp, coins.cpp, and primitives/transaction.* are touched, but the change is a structural safety refactor of the amount type that does not alter what the node accepts, rejects, or how chainstate is maintained.
categories.rationale: Per the validation category's own carve-out, structural refactors passing through validation files without changing validation behavior are excluded; l0rinc did flag a real open question about MoneyRange enforcement in AmountCompression, which the author says is unchanged from master, so no behavioral shift is claimed or shown.

categories.name: wallet
categories.evidence: wallet/coinselection.cpp, spend.cpp, receive.cpp, etc. are heavily touched, but only to adapt to CAmount's explicit-construction and comparison rules (e.g. replacing 0.5*COIN test literals); no change to coin selection, fee bumping, or fund-safety logic itself.
categories.rationale: Mechanical call-site adaptation across wallet code; l0rinc's concern about the COIN/2 test literal was about test-code float imprecision, not a fund-safety change to wallet logic.

uncertainties: Whether validation and wallet should be counted as members given how pervasively CAmount's semantics (initialization, comparison) are used in their core logic, even though no behavior changes are claimed.
Whether the ipc capnp bug (missed write-back) should be treated as this PR introducing-then-fixing its own defect versus a genuine external-facing serialization gap this PR happened to expose.

The PR's ultimate direction (UDL vs multiplication operator, whether to split into a bounded-amount-type PR first) is still unresolved as of the latest push, so priority and reviewability could shift materially with the next design iteration.
result.card: This RFC converts CAmount from a plain int64_t typedef into a real C++ class, closing off a recurring bug class (implicit bool/float conversion, uninitialized amounts, mismatched-width comparisons, nonsensical amount*amount multiplication) that has already caused two prior bugs cited in the description. It is a large (1486/1258 across 184 files), still-evolving draft: the author force-pushed 11 times, most recently on 2026-08-25 to drop the `_sats` literal syntax in favor of a `*sats` multiplication operator after sustained design pushback. Concept ACKs came from sedited and ryanofsky, but l0rinc formally requested changes wanting a smaller, more gradual rollout with a separate bounded-amount type, and maflcko, Sjors, optout21, and purpleKarrot all raised distinct scope or design objections; two smaller preparatory pieces were already split off and merged (#35456, #35372). Because the core approach is still in flux and the latest push invalidates the commits reviewers previously looked at, this is best read as Paused/still-reworking rather than ready for a full line-by-line review. Its highest-value angle is as a utils-category safety improvement to a widely used primitive, with only a narrow, incidental IPC serialization bug fix as a secondary concrete benefit; other touched areas (wallet, mempool, mining, rpc, p2p, validation) are affected only through mechanical call-site adaptation.
